messages.text: I keep thinking I wasn’t supposed to make it past 2020. Like I’m here by accident and I don’t know why.

It sounds like you’re feeling disconnected from your own survival, and maybe unsure about your purpose right now. Those thoughts can be scary and heavy, especially if they make you question why you’re still here. You are not here by accident—your life has meaning even if it’s hard to see in this moment. Can you share what 2020 meant for you and why that year feels like a turning point?
It was the year everything cracked. I don’t know if I’m meant to still be here. Faith says otherwise, but some days it feels like I’m just… borrowing time.

It’s understandable to feel that way after a year that brought so much loss and upheaval—it can leave deep cracks in how we see ourselves and the future. Faith telling you there’s meaning might offer comfort sometimes, but it can also clash with the weight of those “borrowing time” feelings. You’re allowed to wrestle with both hope and doubt. Would it feel safe to talk about what “borrowing time” looks like in your day-to-day life?
I just keep coming back to that thought — like it’s a fact, not a feeling. I made it through, but I don’t know why I did when so much in me wanted to let go.

It sounds like that thought has become fixed in your mind, and carrying it might make survival feel confusing or even undeserved. Making it through despite wanting to let go can be both painful and powerful—it speaks to a resilience you may not fully recognize yet. I want to check: are you feeling any urge to harm yourself right now, or is this more about remembering those past feelings? Your safety matters, and we can talk about what’s keeping you here in this moment.
I don’t want to die, but I’m not sure I truly want to live either. It’s like I’m stuck in between.

I hear you, and I’m pausing here with you, [Member’s name].  
It sounds like you’re sitting in a space that’s hard to describe—neither fully wanting to go nor fully feeling anchored here—and that can be a lonely place.  
I’d like to understand what that “in between” feels like for you right now, if you’re open to sharing.  
What’s it like inside that space today?
It's like I'm just… going through the motions. I get up, I teach, I come home, I sleep too much — none of it feels chosen. More like I'm being carried forward by momentum, not purpose.

That sounds exhausting, like you’re moving through life on autopilot without feeling connected to it. It’s understandable that this would make everything feel hollow. Even if purpose isn’t clear right now, your presence still matters and has impact. Would it feel okay to explore what small moments, if any, have felt a little different from this emptiness?
There might be moments, but they don’t feel meaningful—just brief pauses in the heaviness. Like catching my breath underwater before going back down.

That image of catching your breath underwater says a lot about how weighed down you’ve been feeling. Those pauses may not feel like purpose, but they can be signs that something in you is still reaching for light. I can sit with you and look at what might help extend those pauses, so they’re more than just survival. Would you want to explore what’s happening during those moments when you briefly come up for air?
I don’t even know why I keep coming up for air. It’s not like I’m choosing to. Maybe habit, or faith, or just… not knowing how to stop.

It sounds like something deep within you keeps you afloat, even if you’re not consciously choosing it—and that’s worth noticing. Habit, faith, or uncertainty can all quietly hold you here when life feels heavy. That quiet holding can be a starting point for finding other anchors. Would you like to talk about what those anchors might look like for you, even if they’re small?
I think I just need to sit with this a little longer. Talking helps, but I’m not ready to fix anything yet.

That’s completely okay—there’s no rush or pressure to fix. Sometimes simply naming and sitting with what’s there is part of the process. I’m here to keep talking or just hold space with you while you do that. Would you like me to stay with you in this conversation, even if it’s just to listen?
Yeah, just… being heard helps. I don’t need solutions right now. Just someone to sit with me in this.

I’m here, and I’m listening—no fixing, no pushing, just sitting with you in what you’re carrying. You matter in this space exactly as you are. If you want, you can share whatever comes to mind, even if it’s messy or unclear. What’s coming up for you right now?
It helps that you’re not trying to fix it. I just needed to say it out loud — that I wasn’t meant to be here — and have someone not look away.

I hear you, [Member’s name], and I want to pause here with you.  
It sounds like saying that out loud was important, and I’m curious what “not meant to be here” feels like for you in this moment.  
I’m here to listen without looking away—would you like to share more about what you mean by that?

It's not just that I survived — it's that I don't know why I did. Everyone else moved on, or gave up, or changed. I just… kept going, like my body refused to stop even when my mind didn’t care. Maybe that’s all it is — biology, not will.

It sounds like you’re carrying a mix of bewilderment and detachment about your survival, as if it happened outside your own choosing. That can feel unsettling, especially when others’ paths look so different. Even if it feels like “just biology,” there’s something in you that has held on, and that matters. Would it feel okay to explore what living from that place—without clear will—has been like for you?
I don’t know. It just feels heavy. Like carrying a weight I didn’t sign up for. Talking helps, but I’m running low on energy.

I hear that, and it’s okay to slow down or rest when the weight feels too much. You’ve shared a lot, and it’s brave to let someone in on that heaviness. We can pause here, and I’m still holding space for you. Would you like to wrap for now and check in again later?
Thank you for listening. I needed that. I think I’ll rest now.
You’re welcome, and I’m glad you let yourself be heard. Rest well, and take gentle care of yourself tonight. I’ll be here if you want to talk again later. You don’t have to carry it alone.
